anatomyData.name: Frontal Bone
anatomyData.description: Forms the forehead and upper part of the eye sockets. Contains the frontal sinuses.
anatomyData.function: Protects the frontal lobe of the brain

quiz.question: Which bone forms the forehead and upper eye sockets?

anatomyData.name: Parietal Bones
anatomyData.description: Paired bones forming the superior and lateral sides of the skull.
anatomyData.location: Top and sides of the cranial cavity
anatomyData.function: Protect the parietal lobes and form the roof of the skull

quiz.question: Which paired bones form the roof and upper sides of the skull?

anatomyData.name: Temporal Bones
anatomyData.description: House structures of the inner and middle ear; form the sides and base of the skull.
anatomyData.location: Lower lateral sides of the skull
anatomyData.function: Protect the temporal lobes and support hearing structures

quiz.question: Which bones contain the ear structures and form the sides of the skull base?

anatomyData.name: Occipital Bone
anatomyData.description: Forms the back and base of the skull. Contains the foramen magnum.
anatomyData.function: Protects the occipital lobe and surrounds the foramen magnum for spinal cord passage

quiz.question: Which bone forms the back of the skull and contains the foramen magnum?

anatomyData.name: Sphenoid Bone
anatomyData.description: Butterfly-shaped bone that forms part of the base of the skull and eye sockets.
anatomyData.location: Central skull, anterior to the temporal bones
anatomyData.function: Connects cranial bones and houses the pituitary gland

quiz.question: Which butterfly-shaped bone forms part of the skull base and houses the pituitary gland?

anatomyData.name: Ethmoid Bone
anatomyData.description: Lightweight spongy bone forming part of the nasal cavity and eye sockets.
anatomyData.location: Between the eyes, anterior to the sphenoid
anatomyData.function: Forms part of the nasal septum and supports the olfactory structures

quiz.question: Which bone helps form the nasal septum and supports the olfactory system?

anatomyData.name: Mandible
anatomyData.description: The lower jawbone, largest and strongest facial bone.
anatomyData.function: Supports lower teeth and enables chewing and speech

quiz.question: Which bone forms the lower jaw and holds the lower teeth?

anatomyData.name: Maxillae
anatomyData.description: Paired bones forming the upper jaw and parts of the eye sockets and nasal cavity.
anatomyData.function: Support upper teeth and form part of the hard palate

quiz.question: Which paired bones form the upper jaw and support the upper teeth?

anatomyData.name: Zygomatic Bones
anatomyData.description: Cheekbones; form the prominence of the cheeks and part of the eye sockets.
anatomyData.function: Provide attachment for facial muscles and protect the eyes

quiz.question: Which bones are commonly known as the cheekbones?

anatomyData.name: Nasal Bones
anatomyData.description: Small rectangular bones forming the bridge of the nose.
anatomyData.function: Support cartilage that shapes the lower nose

quiz.question: Which small paired bones form the bridge of the nose?

anatomyData.name: Lacrimal Bones
anatomyData.description: Small, fragile bones forming part of the medial wall of the orbit.
anatomyData.location: Inner corner of the eye sockets
anatomyData.function: House the nasolacrimal canal for tear drainage

quiz.question: Which bones contain the tear ducts in the inner corner of the eye sockets?

anatomyData.name: Palatine Bones
anatomyData.description: L-shaped bones forming the posterior hard palate and part of the nasal cavity and orbit.
anatomyData.function: Help form the roof of the mouth and nasal passages

quiz.question: Which paired bones form the back of the hard palate?

anatomyData.name: Inferior Nasal Conchae
anatomyData.description: Curved bones projecting from the lateral walls of the nasal cavity.
anatomyData.function: Increase surface area to warm and humidify inhaled air

quiz.question: Which bones project from the lateral walls of the nasal cavity to help warm and humidify air?

anatomyData.name: Vomer
anatomyData.description: Thin, flat bone forming the lower part of the nasal septum.
anatomyData.function: Separates the left and right nasal passages

quiz.question: Which bone forms the lower portion of the nasal septum?
